newsitem.title: UK: BT shares marked higher after MCI deal.
newsitem.headline: BT shares marked higher after MCI deal.

text.p: Shares in British Telecom rose sharply in pre-market trade on Monday, after Sunday's confirmation of the company's $20 billion merger plan with MCI Communications.
BT shares were quoted 26-1/2p higher at 377-1/2 by 0809 GMT, with trading volume already reaching 3.6 million shares.

Earlier, traders said the stock was likely to be volatile on Monday as the market digested the implications of what will be the largest ever acquisition by a UK company, assuming it is approved by regulatory authorities on both sides of the Atlantic.
One analyst said the merger should be worth about 50p on BT shares, based on the value of the promised special dividend and an increased rate of dividend growth.
"It is not difficult to work out what the impact on the shares should be," said Jim McCafferty, analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"The 0.5 percent rise in the dividend growth rate should be worth 20p on the share price and the 35p special dividend should be worth about 30p, given the time value of money."
The Hoare Govett analyst said the merger should be positive longer-term for BT shares since it exposed the company to higher earnings growth opportunities.
"It is positive for BT shareholders and positive for the sector," McCafferty said.

The cost of the deal to BT, and the dilutive effect of the huge number of new shares it will issue to MCI shareholders, were the main negative implications but the industrial logic of the trans-Atlantic telecoms linkup was compelling for analysts.

"BT has exploited its advantage by building onto the relationship it has already established with MCI to make itself the first European company with a foothold in the U.S. telecoms services industry," said John Clarke, analyst at Daiwa Europe.
"The main point is that BT has an opportunity to keep a step ahead of potential European rivals. It will be some time before France Telecom and Deutsche Telecom can do the same for Sprint."
By the official start of trading at 0830 GMT, BT shares were up 23-1/2p at 374-1/2 in heavy trading of 5.8 million shares.
